name: barcode-zero never matches
why: The all-zero detector is the whole finding: without it rows B and I lose their error. Must fail on the per-cell map.
grep: each cell carries exactly its finding

name: barcode-zero matches any barcode with a zero
why: A looser test (a zero anywhere, not every digit) flags the valid barcodes of rows A, E, F, G and H. Must fail on the per-cell map, which pins the near misses too.
grep: each cell carries exactly its finding

name: barcode-missing also flags "[none]"
why: "[none]" is MusicBrainz's known absence (formatBarcode()), not a missing value. Reading the cell's text as empty-or-[none] flags row D. Must fail on the per-cell map.
grep: each cell carries exactly its finding

name: catno-missing counts "[no label]" as a label
why: "[no label]" marks a release known to have no label, so no catalog number is owed. Without the MBID check row F is flagged. Must fail on the per-cell map.
grep: each cell carries exactly its finding

name: catno-missing ignores the Label cell
why: An empty Catalog# cell alone is no finding: row G has no label at all. Must fail on the per-cell map.
grep: each cell carries exactly its finding

name: release-event-none ignores the Country cell
why: A release with a country but no date has a release event. Reading the Date cell alone flags row J (GB, no date). Must fail on the per-cell map.
grep: each cell carries exactly its finding

name: release-event-none flags both Country/Date and Date
why: The split pages keep the source Country/Date column beside Country and Date, so a cols() that takes both puts one finding in two columns of the row (the 📊 ticks would then AND). Must fail on the per-cell map.
grep: each cell carries exactly its finding

name: a heading row counts as a release row
why: _rcIsReleaseRow() keeps note and heading rows of a release list from being flagged for empty cells. The fixture has no such row, so nothing sees it. Recorded as a pass; a fixture with a colspan note row inside a release table would catch it.
grep: each cell carries exactly its finding

name: the barcode-zero tint setting is ignored
why: The tint must follow sa_findings_tint_barcode_zero. Must fail on the tint-settings test.
grep: the tint settings turn the paint off

name: barcode-zero is a warning
why: An all-zero barcode is an error (red ❌, the ERROR menu). Must fail on the menu test, which looks for it under ERROR.
grep: the menus list each finding under its level
